newsitem.title: USA: US West Coast lt. crudes prices rise, diffs idle.
newsitem.headline: US West Coast lt. crudes prices rise, diffs idle.

text.p: U.S West Coast light crudes advanced with West Texas Intermediate (WTI) Tuesday, with differentials idle as players evaluated their supply needs for April, traders said.
Discounts for Alaska North Slope (ANS) crude remained at -$0.90 cents under WTI, with BP Oil Co declining to offer a price for the grade. Outright prices stood $19.50/19.70.
"We're gonna watch arbs and check that are volume balances are correct," a seller said.
Buyers of Line 63 attended the auction of light California grades from the Elk Hills Naval Petroleum Reserve on Tuesday.

Line 63 prices stood unchanged at postings plus $0.95 - $1.05, while the market waited to see how Elk Hills was distributed among refiners. Elk Hills crudes, produced in the middle of the state, are components of blended Line 63, which is shipped to Los Angeles refineries.
Kern River heavy crude prices fell, after a major California oil company lowered postings 50 cents late Monday, but no new deals were done.
